tasks.short: Demonstrate equipment to customers and explain how it works, look up specifications and manuals, and give the customer the instructions to take home.

steps.what: Parts salesperson demonstrates equipment to customers and explains its functioning
Parts salesperson looks up specifications in paper manuals and binders
Parts salesperson copies the instructions for the customer

tasks.design: Each product in the shop system ({ECOMMERCE}) links to the maker's specifications, manual and instruction video, so the salesperson finds them on the counter screen instead of in binders. Customers get a QR code to the manual and video instead of a photocopy. Demonstrating and explaining stay with the salesperson.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manuals sat in binders and were photocopied for customers.
tasks.enabler_now: Product data from makers include manuals and videos linked in shop systems.
tasks.still_hard: Older equipment has no digital manual.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a customer the one trick that makes the tool safe to use.

reach.learn: Whether fewer customers return with how-to questions.

evidence.claim: Shop systems can link products to makers' manuals and videos.

assumptions: Boundary: from customer interest to instructions given; the sale is outside.
Input contract: product data from makers; fallback is binders.
Customers open the QR code in about the time they read a copy; no added customer time.
research_questions: Do how-to questions after the sale fall?

incremental.description: Parts salesperson reports products without a linked manual.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few products with manuals; high: a large range of equipment.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the delivery route, deliver parts to customers, pick up parts at suppliers, and get delivery notes signed and handed in.

steps.what: Parts salesperson plans the delivery route from the order list
Parts salesperson delivers parts to customers
Parts salesperson picks up parts at suppliers
Parts salesperson gets paper delivery notes signed and hands them in

tasks.design: Delivery orders from the shop system ({ERP}) go into a route planner on the driver's phone, which orders stops by address. Customers sign on the phone, and the signature and photo go back to the order as proof of delivery instead of paper notes handed in later. Driving, delivering and picking up stay with the salesperson; the app's location is used for the route, not to rate the driver.
tasks.previous_blocker: Routes were planned on paper and delivery notes carried back to the shop.
tasks.enabler_now: Route planners and phone proof of delivery are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent orders break the planned route.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which garage needs the part before noon or loses the job.

reach.learn: Whether proofs of delivery arrive the same day.

evidence.claim: Route planners and phone proof of delivery are standard delivery tools.
Tools fit to monitor staff need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from delivery orders to delivery proof; invoicing is outside.
Input contract: orders in the shop system; fallback is paper notes.
Customers sign on the phone in about the time a paper note took; no added customer time.
Driving and delivering do not change.

incremental.description: Parts salesperson fixes addresses the planner cannot find.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few stops a day; high: many stops on a long route.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The parts salesperson keeps demonstrating equipment and delivering parts; binders, photocopies, paper routes and delivery notes shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A salesperson with more time for customers at the counter.
